title: Ask journal: friction snapshots & prototyping notes
summary: Working notebook capturing micro-threads from recent customer interviews, short friction snapshots with severity notes, and three lightweight prototype ideas we can ship as experiments. Not a finished product doc — intended as an actionable input to product triage and a reference for engineering pairing sessions.
body:
Context and purpose:
This doc collects customer-reported friction patterns from Oct-Nov 2026 calls and support threads. Goal: surface low-effort, high-impact fixes and one lean prototype per theme to validate whether the signal is operational (telemetry can detect) and productizable.

How I collected this: quick call notes, CS Zendesk snippets, and two partner interviews. I focused on requests that are either reproducible via logs or trivially prototypable in a week.

Top-level themes (raw):
- Observability gaps: token-level cost attribution often too coarse for multi-route customers; customers want per-function breakdowns for calls using function-calling or multi-turn chat.
- Unexpected model fallthroughs: when private deployment runs out of capacity, customers see cryptic 503s rather than graceful fallback to smaller model variants.
- Prefix cache unpredictability: TTL and invalidation semantics not well communicated; customers report stale outputs after prompt template edits.
- Embedding drift: users report drop in semantic recall after we rotated model family; not clearly surfaced or easy to roll back.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Prioritize fixes that we can toggle with runtime flags — allows rapid A/B collects.
- Ask infra for a 2-week sample of fallthrough events to estimate rate and affected customers.
- Consider temporary docs snippet for private customers describing cache semantics.

Friction snapshots (severity + reproducibility):
1) Account: Telos Health (midmarket)
   Severity: High (production latency + customer-facing errors)
   Reproducible: Yes (logs show fallback -> 503 in three windows)
   Reported impact: Several scheduled reports failed; customers patch by retrying which doubles costs.
   Key ask: graceful fallback path + visibility that a fallback occurred.

2) Account: MonoAI (startup)
   Severity: Medium
   Reproducible: Partially (seen in canary night windows)
   Reported impact: Confusing partial responses when prefix-cache returns older KV; developers had to clear cache manually.
   Key ask: clearer cache TTL controls and a manual invalidate API.

3) Account: EdgeBank (enterprise)
   Severity: Low
   Reproducible: Yes
   Reported impact: Embedding mismatch after model swap; offline re-embedding is heavy.
   Key ask: tooling to preview embedding drift and a rollback path for embedding indexes.

Customer snippets (verbatim/short):
customer_snippets: Telos: 'We saw 503s during a busy hour and zero explanation in the logs. Our QA just retries and it kills our budget.'
MonoAI: 'I changed a prompt template and some responses suddenly came from an older behavior — how do I evict that state?'
EdgeBank: 'After you updated the embedder our similarity results fell off. We had no way to preview or revert.'
proposed_quick_fixes: Add a fallback-notice field to response payloads for any automatic model downgrade (runtime flag: response.fallback_reason)
Expose cache control headers for prefix caching (cache_ttl_ms, last_invalidate_ts) in admin response stream
Quick invalidation API: POST /v1/admin/cache/invalidate with simple filter (route_id, prefix_hash)
Telemetry: emit event FALLBACK_OCCURRED with tags {route, model_from, model_to, latency_ms} to existing metrics sink
experimental_prototypes: Canary 1 — graceful-fallback header: add response header and a small UI toggle in Console for customers to opt-in. Target customer: Telos Health. Config snippet: {route: 'reports', fallback_policy: 'smaller-variance', emit_fallback_reason: true}
Canary 2 — manual-prefix-invalidate: quick admin endpoint + small client SDK helper. Measure: time-to-fix and number of manual invalidations per day. Target: MonoAI.
Canary 3 — embedding-preview pipeline: allow customers to re-run a 1% sample of queries against new embedder and surface delta. Offline-only, read-only modal in Console for EdgeBank.
research_questions: What's the roughly weekly rate of automatic fallbacks across hosted vs dedicated customers? (ask infra for event logs for last 8 weeks)
How frequently do customers manually invalidate prefix caches today? Are they using adhoc API calls or redeploys?
Can we cheaply compute embedding drift on a 1% slice to give an early-warning signal? What's the cost per 100k rows?
follow_up_actions: Ethan to request fallback event export from infra by 2026-11-10
Sofia to draft a short support doc explaining cache semantics and suggested workflows — due 2026-11-15
Product to triage quick-fixes during next PD sync (agenda item: 2026-11-18)
Schedule 30m pairing session with MonoAI engineers to prototype invalidate endpoint — target week of 2026-11-22
priority_rationale: Ranked by product of customer impact and ease-of-ship. Graceful fallback and telemetry are high impact, low engineering risk (can be a runtime flag + metric). Cache invalidate API is medium effort but reduces repeated manual fixes; embedding-preview is higher lift, lower immediacy — keep as a Q1 spike for dedicated/private customers.
retrospective_notes: If we ship a fallback notice without telemetry we risk noise. Ensure metrics backfill on rollout day and an initial 48-hour auto-alert. Keep this doc as the living source for follow-ups; convert to a Confluence decision page once we reach consensus.
